prologue.1: Hello, Commander! I’m Robo, your mission assistant.
prologue.2: You are in charge of a small crew on Mars. Our outpost sits in Gale Crater, a giant bowl in the ground with a mountain in the middle.
prologue.3: A supply ship is on its way! It will arrive after Sol 10.
prologue.4: Until then, we must keep three things going: air and water, power, and protection from the Sun’s radiation.
prologue.5: Every choice costs something. There are no perfect answers, only smart ones.
touchdown.narration.1: We made it! The landing dust is settling.
touchdown.narration.2: Look, Commander: that tall mountain is Mount Sharp, and we are standing in Gale Crater. Today is Sol 1.
touchdown.dialogue.robo: A sol is one Martian day. It is a little longer than a day on Earth.
touchdown.dialogue.kai: Everything runs on power: air, heat, even the lights.
touchdown.dialogue.mei: Don’t forget the greenhouse. Plants help us breathe and eat!
touchdown.cargo.solar_extra: We brought extra panels to help generate power.
touchdown.cargo.water_recycler: Our recycler gave us a starting supply boost.
touchdown.cargo.greenhouse_kit: Our greenhouse kit helps us use supplies carefully.
touchdown.question: Where does the first power go?
touchdown.A.label: Air system first
touchdown.B.label: Shield first
touchdown.C.label: Greenhouse lights first
touchdown.A.after: Air first! Breathing comes before everything. We have a little less power now, so we will plan carefully.
touchdown.B.after: The shield is ready to protect us from radiation. The air system can wait a little, but not for long.
touchdown.C.after: Mei’s plants are waking up! Plants give us food and fresh air, but their lights use a lot of power.
touchdown.classroom: Why could we not give the first power to everything?
